purpose: A workbench for evaluating, designing, and operating agentic AI systems — tools, harnesses, loops, workflows, and orchestration frameworks. Single-purpose, client-side, zero accounts. Statuses, caveats, and estimates are stated honestly: planned tools are not counted as shipped, duplicates are flagged, and no tool claims capabilities it does not have.

dimensions.label: Reliability
dimensions.description: Deterministic behavior, repeatability, stable long-run execution, graceful degradation, clear rollback paths.

dimensions.label: Architecture & Contracts
dimensions.description: Schemas, interfaces, domain rules, module boundaries, separation of responsibilities.

dimensions.label: Closed-loop Evaluation
dimensions.description: Automated scoring, feedback cycles, error clustering, traceability, continuous improvement.

dimensions.label: Tooling Integration
dimensions.description: Explicit I/O contracts, retries, rate limits, secure action boundaries, extensibility.

dimensions.label: Workflow & Orchestration
dimensions.description: Planning, acting, evaluating, branching, async execution, parallelism, deterministic handoffs.

dimensions.label: Observability
dimensions.description: Distributed tracing, decision logs, cost monitoring, drift detection, transparency into agent reasoning.

dimensions.label: Safety & Governance
dimensions.description: Budget caps, forbidden actions, human-in-the-loop checkpoints, output validation, compliance boundaries.

dimensions.label: Scale & Maintainability
dimensions.description: Modular architecture, versioning, CI/CD compatibility, reproducibility, low operational overhead.

focuses.evaluate: Evaluate: benchmarks, evals, judges, and diagnostics
focuses.design: Design: harnesses, schemas, context & state engineering
focuses.operate: Operate: cost, capacity, latency, and proxy infrastructure

decisionLog.description: Ordered agent decisions with stated confidence and the observed outcome, for calibration analysis.

root.decisions: decision[] (required, non-empty; a bare array is also accepted)

behaviorSnapshot.description: Daily aggregate metrics for an agent, used to compare a baseline window against a recent window.

point.metrics: object of metricName -> number; keys should be consistent across points

apps.name: Adversarial Edge-Case Red-Teamer
apps.description: Two honest layers: a static review of the prompt text for known weak patterns (instruction hierarchy, delimiters, tool scope, refusal language, PII handling) and an optional live probe that sends attack vectors to a model with your key and reports which bypassed.
apps.notes: Static review is labeled heuristic text analysis — not a vulnerability scan. Live probe uses substring detection and needs a Gemini key; results are indicative, not a security guarantee.

apps.name: AI Infra Router & SOW Generator
apps.description: Deterministic build-vs-buy framework with a fully transparent cost model: every assumption (managed $/M, GPU $/hr, tok/s per GPU, utilization, SRE) is an editable input, outputs include a ±30% sensitivity range, a client-side PII scrubber (email, IP, SSN, phone, keys, cards), and a labeled SOW draft template.
apps.notes: Planning estimates only — verify against current vendor pricing. The generated SOW is a DRAFT template with open questions, not an approved specification.

apps.name: Agent Behavior Drift Monitor
apps.description: Evaluates time-series metrics (behaviorSnapshot v1 schema) for baseline vs. recent drift across daily aggregates, highlighting latency and error-rate divergence.
apps.notes: Runs 100% locally on user-provided behaviorSnapshot time-series data. Calculates statistical mean and deviation drift; does not connect to live monitoring backends.

apps.name: Context Compression Benchmarker
apps.description: Compresses your actual text with gzip (lossless), keep-newest trimming, and dedup+stopword stripping; measures real ratios and lexical retention. Optional live LLM summary row with a key.
apps.notes: Retention is lexical coverage only — a floor, not semantic fidelity. The LLM summary row needs a Gemini key and is subject to free-tier rate limits.

apps.name: Context Budgeting & Compactor
apps.description: Fits agent context into a token budget using lossless gzip, keep-newest line trimming, chat-turn trim, and consecutive-duplicate removal — each strategy with an audit of exactly what was dropped and a lexical retention estimate.
apps.notes: Lossless gzip ratio estimates byte savings; token budget counts use lexical word approximation (~1.33 tokens/word), not model-specific BPE tokenizers.

apps.name: Context Firewall & Hand-off Generator
apps.description: Strips trace noise from an agent chat (system echoes, tool-call internals, ISO timestamps, consecutive duplicates) and redacts PII by field policy (email, phone, IP, SSN, keys, cards), producing a compact, deterministic JSON hand-off payload with a full strip/redact audit log and SHA-256 hash.
apps.notes: Redaction is regex-based; tune patterns for your own PII classes. The hash is a corruption check, not a MAC.

apps.name: Decision Log Analyzer
apps.description: Parses structured decisionLog v1 schemas to evaluate agent confidence-vs-outcome calibration, identify failure hotspots by step type, and compute blended cost-per-decision.
apps.notes: Client-side analysis of decisionLog JSON exports. Calibration accuracy and cost calculations depend entirely on the completeness of exported decision logs.

apps.name: EdgeGuard AI
apps.description: Dual-engine hedge router: primary Groq call at t=0, Gemini Flash hedge fired only if the threshold passes, winner takes all, loser aborted via AbortController, hedge timer always cleared. Tracks aborted calls and estimated cost.
apps.notes: Cost estimate assumes output at max tokens (worst case). Real APIs called from your browser with your keys.

apps.name: Eval Run Diff
apps.description: Compare two evaluation runs (golden-set or rubric scores) and surface regressions. Input two result sets; outputs per-sample deltas, aggregate metrics, and a ranked list of biggest changes.
apps.notes: Score comparison uses 5% threshold to classify as regression/improvement. Pass/fail changes always count. Does not account for statistical significance or dataset size. Use to spot obvious regressions before submitting a prompt change to production.

apps.name: Few-Shot Canonical Example Builder
apps.description: Formats exemplar arrays into copy-paste prompt blocks (### EXAMPLES ###, JSON, or XML) with per-example token budgeting, whole-block budget checks, exact-duplicate detection, and one-click copy.
apps.notes: Token budgeting uses heuristic word-multiplier estimation (~1.33 tok/word); formatting and duplicate detection are deterministic.

apps.name: JSON Schema Contract Validator (Subset)
apps.description: Validates a JSON payload against a JSON Schema subset: required, type, enum, pattern, numeric bounds, string length, nested objects, array items, additionalProperties — with a JSONPath violation report. 100% local, deterministic.
apps.notes: Validates a core JSON Schema subset (required, types, bounds, patterns, nested objects/arrays). Does not support $ref, oneOf, allOf, or anyOf.

apps.name: Golden Dataset Test Harness
apps.description: Golden-set regression runner: JSON/CSV ingest, honest local dataset lint (duplicate IDs, missing expected outputs, key coverage), then live parallel runs against Gemini with deep-diff comparison and per-case latency.
apps.notes: Live mode is Gemini-only with a fixed concurrency of 4; no retries or cost tracking. Local lint is dataset integrity only.

apps.name: Governance & Budget Caps
apps.description: Evaluates an agent-usage log against a policy — monthly budget with warning threshold, per-model caps, forbidden actions, HITL escalation triggers, output-validation rules — and produces an enforcement decision per event (ALLOW/WARN/HITL/BLOCK/BLOCK_BUDGET), spend projections, and a violations list.
apps.notes: A policy simulator — it does not enforce anything; wire the same rules into your real gateway. Regex patterns are case-insensitive.

apps.name: Systems Latency & Capacity Profiler
apps.description: Back-of-the-envelope capacity planning math inspired by Jeff Dean's 'Numbers Every Programmer Should Know': models in-flight bytes (bandwidth x RTT via Little's Law), per-request data volume, required bandwidth vs link limits (bits/s converted to bytes/s), IOPS vs disk limits, and a reference latency table.
apps.notes: Client-side calculator based on classic systems heuristics from Jeff Dean's 'Numbers Every Programmer Should Know' (Stanford CS295 talk / canonical gist https://gist.github.com/jboner/2841832). The reference table is fixed, not editable; IOPS assumes one I/O per request; protocol overhead and queueing are ignored. Useful for architectural scoping; not a live network benchmark.

apps.name: LLM-as-a-Judge Rubric Evaluator
apps.description: Grades output against your own rubric via a live Gemini judge (weighted scores with rationale), plus an honest local structural-check mode that refuses to fake rubric grades.
apps.notes: Local structural checks (JSON validity, keywords, code fences, repeated sentences) are shallow; a real rubric grade requires the live judge and a Gemini key.

apps.name: MCP Client Inspector
apps.description: Recursively compiles MCP-style tool definitions into OpenAI-style function schemas or Gemini FunctionDeclarations as you type, handling nested objects, arrays (including arrays of objects), enums, defaults, and required flags.
apps.notes: Input is a custom JSON shape ({name, description, args|parameters} with per-arg required flags), not raw MCP tool definitions. Gemini output follows the FunctionDeclaration OpenAPI-subset (uppercase types, enums, nested objects and array items) but omits `default`; neither output is validated against a live provider API.

apps.name: Multi-LLM Arena & Parallel Tester
apps.description: Fires one prompt at two models in parallel (Gemini + Groq), measuring true streaming TTFT, total latency, tok/s, trigram-dice output similarity, and an LCS diff. Clearly-labeled simulation mode without keys.
apps.notes: Token counts are heuristic (words × 1.33); simulation mode uses placeholder latencies, clearly labeled.

apps.name: Needle in a Haystack Benchmarker
apps.description: Real retrieval sweep: embeds a needle at each context depth, queries the model, and produces a depth-recall curve with a lost-in-the-middle diagnosis. Local mode validates the harness but never fabricates recall numbers.
apps.notes: Filler corpus is 20 sentences repeated; answer matching is substring-based.

apps.name: OpenTelemetry GenAI → agentTrace Converter
apps.description: Transform OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic convention spans into the bench's agentTrace v1 schema. Input OTel JSON; outputs agentTrace spans for use with Agent Trace Inspector. Supports LangChain, LiteLLM, and custom exporters.
apps.notes: Maps OTel GenAI semantic conventions to agentTrace v1 using heuristics for type detection (llm/tool/eval/loop/handoff/plan). Requires input spans with gen_ai.usage.* attributes. Unmapped attributes become attrs{}. Use this to feed production traces into the bench's observability tools.

apps.name: System Prompt Mutation Optimizer
apps.description: Generates deterministic prompt variants (negative constraints, delimiters, structure, compression, output format, persona) and ranks them via transparent local heuristics or a live judge leaderboard.
apps.notes: The local score is a weighted regex checklist — an exploration aid, not a rigorous metric.

apps.name: ReAct Loop Visualizer
apps.description: Parses Thought → Action → Observation trace lines into a color-coded, step-through timeline for inspecting intermediate agent loop steps and spotting stuck loops.
apps.notes: Parses only `Label: content` lines; no JSON tool-call formatting. For debugging traces, not production telemetry.

apps.name: Retry/Backoff & Rate-Limit Simulator
apps.description: Model retry storms, exponential backoff with jitter, and 429 rate-limit handling. Input a request log and policy; outputs retry timeline, cost impact, and success rate.
apps.notes: Retry simulation heuristic: assumes 70% success on first retry, +15% per additional retry. Real systems vary by provider, load, and context. Does not model token-level jitter or adaptive backoff strategies. Use to reason about retry costs and retry storms, then wire into a real gateway.

apps.name: JSON Schema Repair Loop
apps.description: Validates a payload against a JSON Schema subset, classifies every violation, applies targeted auto-repairs (type coercion, close-match enum correction, default insertion, numeric clamping, extra-property stripping), then re-validates up to N passes with a complete repair log. Violations without a safe repair are reported and left unchanged rather than forced.
apps.notes: Repairs are conservative: enum correction only accepts matches within ⌊len/3⌋ case-insensitive edits, missing keys are inserted only from a schema default, and pattern/length/const violations are never auto-repaired. Supports the same JSON Schema subset as the contract validator (no $ref, oneOf, allOf, anyOf).

apps.name: Scratchpad State Manager
apps.description: Wraps agent scratchpad state into a versioned hand-off payload with a real SHA-256 integrity hash (WebCrypto) and a verify path. Runs fully locally.
apps.notes: The hash is keyless — it detects accidental corruption, not malicious tampering.

apps.name: Session Cost Attributor
apps.description: Ingests session traces (agentTrace v1 schema) and builds stacked bar charts attributing spend across sessions, models, and step types (plan vs. tool vs. eval), calculating blended $/1M tokens.
apps.notes: Calculates spend attribution locally from agentTrace JSON logs. Does not connect to billing APIs or cloud provider cost explorers.

apps.name: Tool Permission & Allowlist Designer
apps.description: Define per-tool allowed actions and test an agent trace against them. Specify which tools can call which resources (e.g., "payment-processor can only call stripe.charges.create"). Test violations against a trace.
apps.notes: Access control is modeled as static allowlists with regex patterns for resources. This is a policy designer, not a runtime enforcer — wire the same rules into your gateway or orchestration layer for actual enforcement. Patterns are case-insensitive regex.

apps.name: Agent Trace Inspector
apps.description: Renders nested waterfall charts from agentTrace v1 JSON logs, calculates the critical path (longest root-to-leaf duration chain), shows span types (plan, llm, tool, eval, loop, handoff, act), and aggregates tokens, duration, and cost.
apps.notes: Runs 100% client-side on exported agentTrace JSON; no live ingestion. Totals are plain sums over all spans, so parent spans carrying rolled-up child costs are double-counted. Unknown span types render as 'other'.

apps.name: Workflow Orchestration Designer
apps.description: Designs multi-step agent workflows as typed nodes (plan, act, tool, eval, HITL, handoff, end) with explicit ok/err edges, then runs a deterministic execution simulation — trace, depth, cycle detection, unreachable-node checks — and exports the spec as JSON or a Mermaid flowchart.
apps.notes: Deterministic simulation of the spec — it does not execute real agents. Mermaid export is a flowchart subset; edges to missing nodes are dropped.

apps.name: Token Budget Planner
apps.description: Plan token budgets for multi-turn sessions and concurrent users. Input model pricing, session structure, and parallelism; outputs max tokens/hour, cost per interaction, per-request allowance.
apps.notes: Deterministic budget math based on pricing per 1M tokens, session structure (turns and tokens per turn), and concurrent user load. Outputs utilization percentage, headroom, per-request token allowance, and hourly rate limits.

apps.name: Load Simulator
apps.description: Model concurrent requests, latency profiles, and error rates. Input traffic pattern, response distribution, and endpoint config; outputs throughput, p50/p95/p99 latencies, error rate impact.
apps.notes: Simulates concurrent request load under normal latency distribution. Measures throughput, percentile latencies (p50/p95/p99), error rates, retry overhead, and timeout behavior. Use to validate timeout thresholds and identify bottlenecks.

apps.name: Cost Forecaster
apps.description: Project weekly/monthly spend from current usage patterns. Input daily cost log and growth assumptions; outputs forecast timeline, best/worst-case scenarios, budget alerts.
apps.notes: Projects future spend based on recent daily costs and growth assumptions. Computes baseline trend, applies growth rates, projects weekly and monthly totals with best/worst-case scenarios. Alerts if forecasted spend exceeds budget ceiling.

apps.name: Workflow DAG Validator
apps.description: Validate workflow topology for cycles, missing handlers, unreachable nodes. Input DAG edges and state machine; outputs validity status, detected cycles, isolated components, reachability matrix.
apps.notes: Validates workflow DAG structure: detects cycles via depth-first search, orphaned nodes (unreachable from entry), dangling edges (target not in nodes), and missing exit handlers. Essential for preventing silent workflow failures.

apps.name: Request Queueing Simulator
apps.description: Model queue behavior under load with priorities, timeouts, and backpressure. Input arrival rate, service time, queue limits; outputs queue depth, wait times, rejection rate, SLA violations.
apps.notes: Simulates M/M/1 queue behavior: arrival rate > service rate creates backlog. Models request timeout, max queue depth, rejection when full, and optional priority queueing. Outputs SLA compliance, queue statistics, and capacity recommendations.
